description: Bonus mental-math patterns and interesting facts

cards.back: A number is divisible by 3 if sum of its digits is divisible by 3.
A number is divisible by 9 if sum of its digits is divisible by 9.
Difference between alternating digit sums is multiple of 11 (including 0).
For n ending in 5, square by multiplying first part by next integer then append 25.
For ab, result is a (a+b) b with carry if needed.
It keeps factorial pattern consistent with n! = n*(n-1)! and combinatorics formulas.
Pi cannot be written as a ratio of integers and has non-repeating infinite decimals.
Euclid proved there are infinitely many primes.
Digit sums mod 9 can quickly check arithmetic for likely mistakes.
2^10 is 1024, close to 1000; useful for quick estimates.

cards.front: Sum of first n odd numbers

cards.back: Repeatedly sum digits until one digit remains; useful for mod 9 patterns.
Ratio of consecutive Fibonacci numbers approaches golden ratio about 1.618.
x percent means x/100; reduce to simplest terms.
